step_by_step_reasoning:
1. **Graph Meta:** Extract architecture title from transcript (trade data processing and retrieval using AWS OpenSearch for Cybex/Cybage), video URL, relevant categories, and operational notes.
2. **Nodes Definition:** Map visual components in the Data Ingestion and Data Retrieval boundary boxes. Use exact service identifiers from the valid vocabulary list:
   - Data Ingestion: S3 (Raw Data), Lambda (Validation), S3 (Validated Data), Lambda (Processing), OpenSearch (Data Ingestion, running on Graviton2 instances).
   - Data Retrieval: User (UserConsumerWebMobile), Front-End Application (ThirdParty - Angular), Back-End Application (ThirdParty - Python), OpenSearch (Data Retrieval, running on Graviton2 instances), Amazon RDS, Amazon S3 (Data Retrieval), Amazon SES.
3. **Edges Definition & Flow Identification:**
   - Flow 0 (Data Ingestion Pipeline): Raw data uploaded to S3 -> Validation Lambda -> Validated data uploaded to S3 -> Processing Lambda -> OpenSearch cluster (Graviton2).
   - Flow 1 (Web Application Retrieval): User -> Front-End (Angular) -> User -> Back-End (Python).
   - Flow 2 (Mobile & Backend Data Querying / Large Report Handling): User/Mobile -> Back-End (Python) -> OpenSearch / RDS / S3. Large reports generate pre-signed URLs sent via Amazon SES.

graph.name: Trade Data Processing and Retrieval Architecture with AWS OpenSearch
graph.categories: Data Processing, Search & Analytics, Event-Driven Architecture
graph.notes: Data processing and retrieval architecture built for Cybex/Cybage to handle ~5 billion records. Features an event-driven ingestion pipeline (S3, Lambda, OpenSearch on Graviton2) and dual retrieval paths via web (Angular FE) and mobile/API (Python BE) querying OpenSearch, RDS, S3, and SES for report notifications.

nodes.name: Amazon S3 (Raw Data)
nodes.notes: Stores uploaded raw trade data files in CSV or Excel formats.

nodes.name: AWS Lambda (Validation)
nodes.notes: Triggered by raw data uploads to validate contents and highlight discrepancies.

nodes.name: Amazon S3 (Validated Data)
nodes.notes: Stores validated copies of data in a dedicated S3 location.

nodes.name: AWS Lambda (Processing)
nodes.notes: Triggered by validated data to process payloads and ingest into OpenSearch.

nodes.name: AWS OpenSearch (Data Ingestion)
nodes.notes: Ingests processed data; utilizes Graviton2 instances, query templates, index mapping, and aggregated reporting layers.

nodes.name: User
nodes.notes: End users accessing export-import trade data via web browser or mobile app.

nodes.name: Front-End Application
nodes.notes: Angular-based web front-end application running in the user's browser.

nodes.name: Back-End Application
nodes.notes: Python-based back-end application servicing business logic and data layer access.

nodes.name: AWS OpenSearch (Data Retrieval)
nodes.notes: OpenSearch cluster running on Graviton2 instances providing 2-4 second response times across ~5B records.

nodes.name: Amazon RDS
nodes.notes: Relational database providing relational data querying capabilities to the back-end.

nodes.name: Amazon S3 (Data Retrieval)
nodes.notes: Stores large generated reports (over 10,000 records) accessible via pre-signed URLs.

nodes.name: Amazon SES
nodes.notes: Sends email intimations containing pre-signed URLs to users for downloading large reports.

edges.notes: Raw data upload triggers validation Lambda function.
Validation Lambda writes validated copy of data into S3.
Validated data upload triggers processing Lambda function.
Processing Lambda ingests processed data into OpenSearch cluster.
User sends web request to Angular front-end application.
Front-end application returns response to user browser.
Web browser forwards application request to Python back-end application.
Mobile application sends direct requests to Python back-end application.
Back-end queries relational database layer in Amazon RDS.
Back-end uploads large reports (>10,000 records) to S3 bucket.
Back-end application sends query results back to user.
SES delivers email intimation with pre-signed URL for S3 report download.
